location: Design Notes > Worker interface (spec.json / result file)
issue: The spec defines the content of spec.json and the result file but not where they are written, how they are named per job/version/engine, their permissions, or who deletes them. The cleanup rule covers only the lock file, holders dir and step dir. spec.json carries `ctx`, which includes `admin_password`. If it lands in the shared, world-writable LOCK_DIR (chmod 1777 by `_slots_lock`) or another shared /tmp path with default umask, it is world-readable and is never removed. spec.json also lacks `slow_after`, so workers ignore the operator's `--slow-after` for their `browser:<engine>` phase.
implementation_impact: Two implementers will choose different paths. Per-run files pile up in /tmp. A collision between two jobs or versions sharing a name corrupts results, and the credential file leaks. Worker heartbeat thresholds will differ from the version process's.
suggestion: Write both files in a private per-version temp dir (mkdtemp, 0700) named `<engine>.spec.json` / `<engine>.result.json`, and delete it with the lock/holders/step dirs after all workers exit, including on the JobStopped path. Add `slow_after` to spec.json.

location: Always > Child (spawn workers) / Design Notes > Worker interface
issue: Worker stdout and stderr handling is unspecified. If workers inherit stdout, anything they print (the `JOB ...` banner goes to stderr, but stray prints or Playwright driver output may not) lands in the same stream where a direct run without `-o` prints its result JSON, which breaks callers that parse it. If the streams are PIPEs that nobody reads, a chatty worker blocks once the pipe buffer fills, and the barrier waits forever. A worker crash records only the exit code in `browser_notes`, so the traceback that explains a `crash` cell is lost.
implementation_impact: There is a deadlock or corrupted-JSON risk, depending on the implementer's choice. `crash` cells cannot be diagnosed.
suggestion: Specify `stdout=DEVNULL` and stderr redirected to a per-worker file in the worker temp dir. On `crash`, append the last ~300 characters of that file to the `browser_notes` entry next to the exit code.

location: Design Notes > `scenario_spans`; Always > lock ("releases it ... when the scenario ends, before writing its step marker"); Tasks > live test (c)
issue: Span boundaries are never defined relative to lock acquisition, lock release and the barrier. If `start_ns` is taken before the flock is acquired (including lock-wait), BO spans of the two engines overlap by design. If `end_ns` is taken after the fd is closed, the other engine can acquire the lock and stamp its start first. Either way, live test (c) ('no BO-scenario span overlaps the other engine's spans') fails or flakes on a correct implementation.
implementation_impact: Live (c) produces false failures or intermittent flakes, and the unit tests cannot pin the behavior.
suggestion: Define the span as `start_ns` taken after the lock is acquired (after lock-wait) and `end_ns` taken before the fd is closed. The order is then: acquire, start_ns, run, end_ns, remove holder marker, close fd, write step marker. Test that order with the real-flock thread test.

location: Design Notes > Worker interface (result schema) / Confirmation merge ("`started_at` ... always stay from the lockstep pass")
issue: The result file is `{engine, result: <drive_engine's return>, scenario_spans, timings}`. `drive_engine` returns no `started_at`/`finished_at`, so the lockstep pass's timestamps must come from the version process. The spec does not say whether they are spawn and reap times (which include interpreter start, Playwright import and the reap poll latency) or values the worker stamps. It also does not say what a `crash` cell carries. The contract says a crashed cell has `started_at` = admission time and null engine fields.
implementation_impact: `started_at`/`finished_at`/`wall_clock` vary between implementations. AC 1's overlap check (`max(started_at) < min(finished_at)`) becomes trivially true with spawn/reap stamps. A crash cell may carry non-null timestamps that the contract forbids.
suggestion: Add `started_at`/`finished_at` (UTC ISO, stamped by the worker around `drive_engine`) to the result schema. State that a `crash` cell leaves both null so that ps-run-layer fills them per the contract.

location: Tasks > live test (c); Acceptance Criteria 1; I/O row Parallel clean
issue: Nothing in the live suite proves that any browser work runs concurrently. In bankwire's tests/e2e, four of the five specs have a BO `goto`, as does the universal smoke. Only `bankwire-checkout-empty-banks-safe` is FO-only. Live (c) checks only non-overlap and step ordering, and AC 1 is satisfied by any spawn-both-then-reap driver. An implementation that takes `LOCK_EX` for every scenario, or that serializes the workers, passes every live check. The 'FO-only spans overlap' property is asserted only against stubs.
implementation_impact: The one property that justifies CAP-7 (cost n slots for shorter browser time) is never verified against a real container and real browsers. A regression to full serialization would ship green.
suggestion: Extend (c): in each version's parallel records, the `bankwire-checkout-empty-banks-safe` spans of the two engines overlap. Name that scenario explicitly in the test, and fail with a clear message if the fixture no longer has an FO-only scenario.

location: Tasks > live test (b); Design Notes > Snapshot and reset in shell
issue: No test checks that the reset actually restores state. The step-55 fault fails on every engine whatever the shop state, so (b)'s identical-findings comparison also passes with a reset that does nothing: a `reset-db` that exits 0 without loading, a `comm -13` with its arguments swapped, or a docroot list that is empty. Unit tests stub the container execs, so the shell commands (DROP DATABASE, dump load, find/sort/comm, php-fpm master discovery) are never checked for effect on any of the three images.
implementation_impact: A broken reset ships undetected. Rerun confirmation then runs against dirty state, which defeats the honesty law it exists to enforce.
suggestion: Add a live check per target version: after `snapshot-db`, insert a sentinel row (for example into `<prefix>configuration`) and create a sentinel file in the docroot, run the reset routine, then assert that the row and file are gone and that the shop answers on `wait-http`.

location: Design Notes > Confirmation passes; Always > Runner (parallel-unconfirmed forcing)
issue: Only findings trigger a sequential pass. Failures that parallel load itself causes get no sequential retry: two browsers plus a PS container on one host can trigger an OOM-killed worker (`crash`), `drive_engine`'s 'gagal setelah launch' (`launch-error`), or step timeouts that make steps inconclusive. These failures also do not force cost-1 sequential admission next time, because only `parallel-unconfirmed` does. A host that cannot sustain two engines therefore repeats parallel `crash`/`launch-error` until the plan reports `blocked-infra`, even though a sequential run would have produced evidence.
implementation_impact: On resource-constrained hosts, versions can become unprovable, and the operator sees `blocked-infra` with no hint that parallel mode is the cause.
suggestion: Either treat a parallel-mode `crash`/`launch-error` cell like a parallel-only failure (one sequential pass after reset, else `parallel-unconfirmed`), or extend the runner's forcing rule to newest records whose `browser_mode` is `parallel` and whose reason is `crash` or `launch-error`. If this needs a contract change, list it under Ask First.

location: Design Notes > Confirmation merge ("`inconclusive` = first pass's ∪ rerun's")
issue: The union keeps parallel-pass inconclusive steps even when the sequential rerun evaluated that same (scenario, step, action) conclusively and it passed. A step that was inconclusive only because of parallel interference, for example a BO step after a login hiccup or a timeout under load, therefore leaves the cell `pass` with a non-empty `inconclusive`. Such a cell is never passing gate-grade and reads as infra cause `inconclusive-steps`. A parallel artifact thus blocks `ready`, while the honesty law filters out parallel artifacts only when they are findings.
implementation_impact: Modules get spurious non-ready verdicts and loops toward `blocked-infra`, even though a sequential pass proved those steps.
suggestion: Keep a first-pass inconclusive entry only when the rerun did not evaluate its key conclusively, so the rerun's conclusive results supersede it. Flag this as a contract wording change ("Inconclusive steps of the rerun are added") under Ask First if needed.

location: Design Notes > Snapshot and reset in shell (`reset-files` ... `cp -r /ps-module-src modules/$MOD_NAME`, no install); Always > Honesty law ("a rerun failure always blocks")
issue: The snapshot docroot list is taken after install, but `reset-files` replaces `modules/$MOD_NAME` with a pristine source copy. Files that install or first use wrote inside the module dir are lost: PS's generated `config.xml`/`config_<iso>.xml`, assets or index files the module compiles on install, and upload dirs it creates. The restored DB says the module is installed, but its install-time files are missing. A rerun failure caused by this is not module behavior, yet the honesty law makes every rerun failure blocking (`fail`, never infra).
implementation_impact: Modules that write into their own directory during install can get false blocking failures in the confirmation pass and in the sequential fallback's later engines.
suggestion: Restore `modules/$MOD_NAME` from a tarball of that directory taken with `snapshot-db` instead of from `/ps-module-src` (only the paths deleted by the pass need care). If the contract's 'fresh copy' must stand, record this as a known divergence in the e2e-quickstart gotchas and in Ask First.

location: Design Notes > Worker interface ("reaps workers within `JOB_STOP_GRACE`"); Always > Child ("forwards SIGTERM")
issue: `stop_job` SIGTERMs every registered pid of the job, workers included, and SIGKILLs the survivors after its own `JOB_STOP_GRACE` (60 s). If the version process also waits up to `JOB_STOP_GRACE` for its workers before teardown, one slow worker uses up the whole grace period, and `stop_job` SIGKILLs the version process before it tears down or writes `DONE rc=stopped`. Workers also receive SIGTERM twice (directly and forwarded). With `_on_sigterm` raising `JobStopped` on each delivery, the second signal can interrupt the first one's cleanup (`browser.close`, the atomic result write, fd release).
implementation_impact: Stopping a job leaves teardown to `stop_job`'s artifact sweep and leaves progress logs without `DONE`. Worker cleanup is nondeterministic.
suggestion: Give the version process a short worker reap window (for example 10 s, then SIGKILL the workers) so that it finishes well inside `stop_job`'s grace. In workers, ignore SIGTERM after the first `JobStopped`, or forward only when the worker is not already registered for direct signalling.

location: Design Notes > Phases (`rerun-seq:<engine>` wraps health check, reset and drive; worker `browser:<engine>` contains lock/barrier waits)
issue: `rerun-seq:<engine>` and the worker's `browser:<engine>` are not wait phases, so `PROGRESS_SLOW_AFTER` (180 s) marks them `SLOW`. `rerun-seq` spans a DB drop and reload, a docroot diff, a full Symfony cache rebuild after `var/cache` is emptied, and a full scenario pass. The parallel `browser:<engine>` now also contains every `lock-wait` and `barrier-wait` for the other engine's BO scenarios. SKILL.md tells the operator that a `SLOW` line means 'diduga macet' and to offer stopping the job.
implementation_impact: Healthy confirmation passes and lockstep passes routinely show `SLOW`, which prompts operators to stop good runs. The docs task adds `rerun-seq:` to 'Pantau run Docker' but does not address its SLOW semantics.
suggestion: Give `rerun-seq:` a phase-specific threshold in `PROGRESS_SLOW_AFTER_PHASE` (or exempt it, since its nested reset phases and steps carry their own bounds). Document in run-phases.md that `browser:<engine>` in parallel mode includes the other engine's BO time.

location: Design Notes > Snapshot and reset in shell (`reset-files` = ... remove every path absent from the list (`comm -13`))
issue: The removal mechanics are underspecified. The spec does not say whether the list holds files only or directories too, whether the current-state listing uses the same `find`/prune/`LC_ALL=C sort` as the snapshot (`comm` needs identically sorted inputs), or how names containing spaces or newlines are handled (a line-based list breaks on them; `comm -z`/`xargs -0` would not). It also does not say whether `modules/$MOD_NAME` is excluded from the diff before or after the `rm -rf`. A files-only list leaves new empty directories behind. An unsorted current listing makes `comm` silently drop or keep the wrong paths.
implementation_impact: The reset can be silently incomplete, or delete wrong paths. Nothing detects it, since no test checks the reset's effect (see the reset-correctness finding).
suggestion: Specify that both listings come from one shared snippet (`find . -path ./var/cache -prune -o -print0 | LC_ALL=C sort -z`), that the diff is `comm -z -13`, that removal is `xargs -0 rm -rf --`, and that `modules/$MOD_NAME` is pruned from both listings.

location: Always > Reset ("used ... by the sequential fallback before each engine after the first"); I/O row Sequential reset fails
issue: In the sequential fallback the reset runs before every later engine, even when the earlier engine drove nothing: a `launch_error` before any scenario, which is not `fail`, so fail-fast does not stop the loop. The shop is then still in the snapshot state, but a failing reset (or a health blip) turns the next engine into `sequential-reset` without need. The parallel side already treats 'a crashed worker drove nothing' as needing no confirmation, so the two paths are inconsistent.
implementation_impact: There are avoidable `sequential-reset` inconclusive cells and extra reset time when the first engine fails to launch.
suggestion: Skip the pre-engine reset when no earlier engine drove a scenario (empty `scenarios_run` / `launch_error` with no spans), and add an I/O row for it.
